# release-monorepo-semantically

> CLI (`monorepo-semantic-release`) that versions, changelogs, tags, and publishes the public packages of a pnpm workspace from conventional commits. It is a set of independent steps, not one command: `report` computes a JSON release context, and every other step consumes that context via `--context` and does one job. The caller (a CI pipeline or shell script) chooses which steps run and in what order.

Full docs: https://github.com/IgorBabkin/release-monorepo-semantically#readme
Config JSON Schema (shipped in the package): `release-monorepo-semantically/release.schema.json` (file: `node_modules/release-monorepo-semantically/dist/release.schema.json`)

## Install

```bash
pnpm add -D release-monorepo-semantically
```

Requires Node >=20.11, a git repository, a root `package.json` with `workspaces` globs, and `name` plus a `major.minor.patch` `version` in every workspace package.

## Canonical pipeline

Run from the workspace root, in this order:

```bash
monorepo-semantic-release check                                      # optional read-only PR preflight
RELEASE_CONTEXT=$(monorepo-semantic-release report)                        # fails if the working tree is dirty
monorepo-semantic-release package-json    --context "$RELEASE_CONTEXT"    # pin internal deps to exact new versions, refresh lockfile
monorepo-semantic-release package-manager --context "$RELEASE_CONTEXT"    # write new versions into package.json files
monorepo-semantic-release changelog       --context "$RELEASE_CONTEXT"    # prepend CHANGELOG.md entries
monorepo-semantic-release vcs             --context "$RELEASE_CONTEXT"    # commit, tag, push
monorepo-semantic-release package-manager publish --context "$RELEASE_CONTEXT"  # optional: pnpm publish
monorepo-semantic-release release-notes   --context "$RELEASE_CONTEXT"    # optional: GitHub Releases via `gh`, needs GITHUB_TOKEN + GITHUB_REPOSITORY
```

- Syntax: `monorepo-semantic-release <step> [action] [--flags]`.
- stdout of `report` is pure JSON; all progress logs go to stderr. Capture it directly, never with `2>&1`.
- Every step accepts `--dry-run` (no file, git, or registry mutation for that step).
- `vcs` actions: default runs `commit`, `tag`, `push`; each is also callable alone (`vcs commit`, `vcs tag`, `vcs push`).
- `package-manager` actions: default writes versions; `publish` publishes. They are separate on purpose.
- `--template <path>` overrides the Handlebars template for `changelog`, `vcs commit`, and `release-notes`. `changelog` also takes `--changelog-name <file>`.
- `check` validates workspace package discovery, all release config, public access for scoped packages, and configured template paths. `report` runs the same validation before computing context.
- GitHub release-notes configuration is optional during preflight; missing credentials or `gh` are warnings. `release-notes` validates its own credentials and CLI before creating releases.
- If nothing needs releasing, `report` emits a context with empty maps and the later steps are no-ops.

## Release context (`report` output)

```json
{
  "releasedVersions": { "@acme/core": "1.3.0" },
  "releasedPackages": [
    { "name": "@acme/core", "dirname": "/abs/path/packages/core", "version": "1.2.4", "isPrivate": false, "dependencies": {}, "devDependencies": {} }
  ],
  "releasedCommits": {
    "@acme/core": [{ "type": "feat", "scope": "@acme/core", "subject": "add thing", "isBreaking": false, "hash": "abc1234..." }]
  }
}
```

`releasedVersions` maps package name to its new version. `releasedPackages[].version` is the version before the release. A commit may also carry `explicitBump` (0 none, 1 patch, 2 minor, 3 major).

## How bumps are computed

- Commits are read per package since its last tag `<package-name>@<version>` (tag format is fixed). With no tag, all history counts.
- Default rules: `feat(<package-name>)` -> minor; `fix(<package-name>)` / `perf(<package-name>)` -> patch; `!` (e.g. `feat(@acme/core)!: ...`) -> major. Only commit headers are read, so a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer in the body is not seen; use `!`. The scope must equal the full package name, e.g. `fix(@acme/core): ...`.
- `docs`, `test`, `ci`, `chore`, `refactor`, `style`, and unparseable messages do not release by default.
- A package whose internal dependency was released in the same run gets at least a minor bump. Packages are processed dependencies-first.
- Priority: major > minor > patch > none.
- Explicit override: `[major]`, `[minor]`, `[patch]`, or `[skip-bump]` in a commit subject replaces the rule-based level for that commit. A scoped tag applies only to the package matching its scope; an unscoped tag applies to every public package.
- Squash merges: by default only a squash commit's subject (e.g. the PR title) is analyzed. Set `report.squash` to `"github"` (GitHub's default squash message) or `{ "detect": "<subject regex>", "entry": "<body line regex>" }` to analyze the commits listed in its body instead. Prefer merge or rebase merges, or a conventional squash title.
- Private packages (`"private": true`) are never released.
- Internal dependency versions are written as exact versions; `workspace:` specifiers and `peerDependencies` are left alone.

## Configuration

Put it in `.release.json` at the workspace root, or under `"release"` in the root `package.json`. When both configure the same step, `.release.json` replaces that step's whole section. CLI flags win over both. Add `"$schema"` for editor validation:

```json
{
  "$schema": "./node_modules/release-monorepo-semantically/dist/release.schema.json",
  "report": {
    "bumps": {
      "patch": [
        { "type": "fix", "scope": "<package>" },
        { "type": "perf", "scope": "<package>" },
        { "type": "docs", "scope": "specs", "packages": "*" }
      ]
    }
  },
  "changelog": { "template": "templates/changelog.hbs", "changelogName": "CHANGELOG.md" },
  "vcs": { "template": "templates/release-commit-msg.hbs" },
  "release-notes": { "repository": "acme/repo" },
  "package-manager": { "kind": "pnpm" }
}
```

Sections: `report`, `package-json`, `package-manager`, `changelog`, `vcs`, `release-notes`. Any section accepts `"dryRun": true`.

`report.bumps.<major|minor|patch>` is a list of matchers `{ type?, scope?, breaking?, packages? }`. A configured level replaces that level's defaults entirely (repeat the defaults you want to keep); unconfigured levels keep their defaults. `scope: "<package>"` means "equals the package being considered". `packages: "*"` releases every public package on a match. `report.squash` is described above.

## Templates

Handlebars. Default templates ship in `dist/features/{changelog/changelog.hbs,vcs/release-commit-msg.hbs,releaseNotes/github-release-notes.hbs}` and are good starting points to copy. Helpers: `now`, `hasBreakingChanges`, `hasFeatures`, `hasFixes`, `hasPerformance`, `hasOthers`, `findBreakingChanges`, `findFeatures`, `findFixes`, `findPerformance`, `findOthers`, `lookup`, `call`.

## Errors

Failures print `[step] ✖ <problem and suggested fix>` to stderr and exit with code 1; GitHub Actions also receives `::error::` annotations. Child-process stderr is decoded to text.

| Code | Meaning / fix |
| --- | --- |
| `DIRTY_WORKING_TREE` | `report` needs a clean tree. Commit or stash first. |
| `INVALID_ROOT_PACKAGE_JSON` | Root `package.json` is missing `workspaces` or is malformed. |
| `INVALID_PACKAGE_JSON` | A workspace package lacks `name` or a `major.minor.patch` `version`. |
| `MISSING_PACKAGE_JSON` | A workspace glob matched a directory with no `package.json`. |
| `INVALID_CONFIG` | A config section fails the schema. The message names the section and field. |
| `PREFLIGHT_VALIDATION_FAILED` | `check` or `report` found unmatched workspace globs, a scoped package without public access, or a missing configured template. |
| `MISSING_PUBLIC_ACCESS` | A scoped package must declare `publishConfig.access: "public"` before it can be published. |
| `MISSING_TEMPLATE` | A configured or command-line template file does not exist. |
| `MISSING_GITHUB_CREDENTIALS` | `release-notes` needs `repository`/`token` config or `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`/`GITHUB_TOKEN`. |
| `GITHUB_CLI_UNAVAILABLE` | `release-notes` needs `gh` on `PATH`. |
| `MISSING_DEPENDENCY_VERSION` | A dependency listed for update isn't declared in the package. |
| `MISSING_CONTROLLER` | No step name was given. |

## Programmatic use

```ts
import { runCli } from 'release-monorepo-semantically';
// Same arguments as the CLI; returns the exit code. Run with process.cwd() at the
// workspace root: git commands use the process working directory.
const exitCode = runCli(['report']);
```
